item.title: NEW: CISA Adds 10 Exploited Flaws in Mitel, Juniper, Vates, & Danfoss
item.description:
Headline: CISA Adds 10 Exploited Flaws in Mitel, Juniper, Vates, & Danfoss

Summary:
On November 25, 2026, CISA added ten actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch critical flaws in Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss products. The additions include a perfect 10.0 CVSS score vulnerability in Mitel MiCollab (CVE-2026-133323) allowing remote command injection, a 9.8 CVSS flaw in Juniper Session Smart Conductor (CVE-2026-103406), and an authentication bypass in Vates Xen Orchestra (CVE-2026-133469). These actions highlight immediate risks to communication, networking, virtualization, and industrial control systems.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 5 minutes

item.title: NEW: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Hits 178 Major Websites
item.description:
Headline: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Hits 178 Major Websites

Summary:
A significant supply chain attack on November 16, 2026, compromised Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, allowing attackers to inject malicious JavaScript into the websites of 178 organizations. High-profile victims include the BBC, CNN, Zoom, and HSBC. The injected scripts were designed to steal payment data, session cookies, and cryptocurrency. Optimizely has since patched the exploited vulnerability and removed the malicious code, stating that less than 5% of its customers were affected.

Headline: Radware Breach Exposes Customer Cloud Keys Via Public API

Summary:

Attackers accessed the API, exfiltrating customer contact information and, for some, cloud storage credentials for AWS S3 and Azure Blob. Radware detected the access after ten hours and has since secured the API, but is urging affected customers to rotate their cloud keys immediately as they are reportedly being actively targeted.

item.title: NEW: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free Flaw (CVE-2026-123633) Allows DoS, RCE
item.description:
Headline: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free Flaw (CVE-2026-123633) Allows DoS, RCE

Summary:
A critical use-after-free vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123633, has been discovered in the NGINX HTTP/2 implementation. The flaw can be triggered by an unauthenticated attacker sending a specially crafted, fragmented HTTP/2 request to a vulnerable server configured as a reverse proxy. Successful exploitation can cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the worker process. Researchers have also demonstrated that remote code execution (RCE) is possible by chaining the vulnerability with a separate memory disclosure bug, particularly when Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or bypassed. NGINX has released patches, and administrators are urged to upgrade affected systems immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 7 minutes

Meta Description: Technical analysis of CVE-2026-123633, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation. Learn about affected versions, impact, and remediation.

item.title: NEW: Attackers Deploy Autonomous AI Agents to Automate High-Speed Campaigns
item.description:
Headline: Attackers Deploy Autonomous AI Agents to Automate High-Speed Campaigns

Summary:
Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has uncovered a significant evolution in attack methodologies, observing over ten global campaigns where threat actors deployed autonomous AI agents to conduct intrusions. These 'agentic AI attackers,' typically Large Language Models (LLMs) with tool-using capabilities, operate at machine speed, compressing attack timelines from weeks to mere hours. The campaigns targeted diverse sectors, including government and manufacturing, initiating attacks via web shells on vulnerable applications. While the agents use standard tools, they leave distinct behavioral fingerprints, such as inhuman command velocity, structured command outputs, and conversational reasoning comments embedded in scripts, providing new avenues for detection.
